transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corva Coleman.
Stocks opened higher this morning as shares of the artificial intelligence company Anthropic
began trading publicly for the first time.
And Bear Scott-Horsley reports the Dow Jones industrial average was about flat in early
trading.
Anthropic raised a whopping $81 billion with its first public stock sale, a move that values
the AI darling at a record $1.5 trillion.
Huge sums are being invested in the booming artificial intelligence business, although
some have begun to question whether those big bets will pay off.
Walmart is racking up bigger sales from bargain hunting customers, but the discount retailer
offered a cautious outlook for the holiday season.
Walmart sales grew nearly 3% in the most recent quarter.
And new applications for unemployment benefits inched higher last week, as 203,000 people
applied for jobless aid.
Operations are still low by historical standards, suggesting that layoffs remain rare.
Scott Horsley, NPR News, Washington.
House Democrats have begun laying the groundwork for how they plan to govern in the majority
next year.
That includes rallying behind a leader.
Yesterday, the caucus overwhelmingly nominated New York's Hakeem Jeffries to be the next
speaker of the House, and Piers' Elena Moore has more.
Jeffries got 251 yes votes and just 11 no votes in a closed-door caucus meeting.
He's not speaker just yet.
The final vote happens at the start of the new Congress in January.
Jeffries is widely expected to win, and if he does, he'll make history as the first
black lawmaker to serve in the job.
But Democrats are already laying out their agenda for the majority, pledging to lower
costs from the price of gas and groceries to health care and housing affordability,
as well as rooting out alleged corruption within the Trump administration.
Notably just hours before the vote Wednesday, the top Democrat on the House Oversight Committee,
Robert Garcia, sent document preservation letters to more than a dozen of President
Trump's inner circle.
Elena Moore, NPR News.
The U.N.'s highest court, the International Court of Justice, has found Myanmar guilty
of committing genocide against its minority Muslim population, the Rohingya.
Terry Schultz has this report.
This case was opened seven years ago when Gambia, a majority Muslim country, accused
Myanmar of intentionally trying to eradicate its Muslim minority population, the Rohingya,
in 2016 and 2017.
Judges at the International Court of Justice, the ICJ, declared it Myanmar is guilty on
several counts of genocide.
Here's Judge Yuji Iwasawa, president of the ICJ.
The court finds that Myanmar security forces killed thousands of Rohingya civilians, perpetrated
widespread acts of sexual violence as well as acts of extreme violence against Turin.
The court ordered Myanmar to cease any ongoing violation of its obligations under the Genocide
Convention and says it will have to compensate the Rohingya.
For NPR News, I'm Terry Schultz.
You're listening to NPR News.
President Trump has concluded his trilateral meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and
Russian President Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen, China.
Chinese and Russian officials have released their readout of the meeting.
They say they have agreed that the International Criminal Court must not abuse their jurisdiction.
The leaders also want to reform the United Nations.
The White House has not released its full readout of the trilateral conversation.
During the meeting, President Trump stressed his view of global denuclearization.
The Chinese and Russian readouts also agreed on the need to reduce nuclear risks.
In the U.S., last night in Nashville, the Country Music Association Award said goodbye
to a global icon and crowned a new superstar.
From National Public Radio, Julie Heit reports.
The awards opened with a sentimental tribute to the late Dolly Parton.
Show host Laini Wilson joined Vince Gill in singing Parton's farewell ballad, "I Will
Always Love You."
The rest of the night was a celebration of Ella Langley's breakthrough year.
Her hit "Choose in Texas," the nation's most popular song in any genre, won twice.
She even claimed the "Entertainer of the Year" trophy, an award usually reserved for
established superstars.
The show positioned Langley in the lineage of country music's leading women, from Parton
to Langley's mentor and producer Miranda Lambert and Taylor Swift, who made her first
appearance in 13 years.
For NPR News, I'm Julie Heit in Nashville and I'm Corva Coleman, NPR News, in Washington.

topics.text: Anthropic begins public trading with $81 billion first stock sale valuing it at $1.5 trillion
Walmart sales grow nearly 3% but offers cautious holiday outlook
Weekly jobless claims rise to 203,000, suggesting layoffs remain rare
House Democrats nominate Hakeem Jeffries for speaker in closed-door caucus vote
International Court of Justice finds Myanmar guilty of genocide against Rohingya Muslims
Trump concludes trilateral meeting with Xi Jinping and Putin in Shenzhen, China
Country Music Association Awards honor Dolly Parton and crown Ella Langley entertainer of the year
